1: :mod:`!shutil` --- High-level file operations
2: =============================================
3: 
4: .. module:: shutil
5:    :synopsis: High-level file operations, including copying.
6: 
7: .. sectionauthor:: Fred L. Drake, Jr. <fdrake@acm.org>
8: .. partly based on the docstrings
9: 
10: **Source code:** :source:`Lib/shutil.py`
11: 
12: .. index::
13:    single: file; copying
14:    single: copying files
15: 
16: --------------
17: 
18: The :mod:`shutil` module offers a number of high-level operations on files and
19: collections of files.  In particular, functions are provided  which support file
20: copying and removal. For operations on individual files, see also the
21: :mod:`os` module.
22: 
23: .. warning::
24: 
25:    Even the higher-level file copying functions (:func:`shutil.copy`,
26:    :func:`shutil.copy2`) cannot copy all file metadata.
27: 
28:    On POSIX platforms, this means that file owner and group are lost as well
29:    as ACLs.  On Mac OS, the resource fork and other metadata are not used.
30:    This means that resources will be lost and file type and creator codes will
31:    not be correct. On Windows, file owners, ACLs and alternate data streams
32:    are not copied.
33: 
34: 
35: .. _file-operations:
36: 
37: Directory and files operations
38: ------------------------------
39: 
40: .. function:: copyfileobj(fsrc, fdst[, length])
41: 
42:    Copy the contents of the :term:`file-like object <file object>` *fsrc* to the file-like object *fdst*.
43:    The integer *length*, if given, is the buffer size. In particular, a negative
44:    *length* value means to copy the data without looping over the source data in
45:    chunks; by default the data is read in chunks to avoid uncontrolled memory
46:    consumption. Note that if the current file position of the *fsrc* object is not
47:    0, only the contents from the current file position to the end of the file will
48:    be copied.
49: 
50: 
51: .. function:: copyfile(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True)
52: 
53:    Copy the contents (no metadata) of the file named *src* to a file named
54:    *dst* and return *dst* in the most efficient way possible.
55:    *src* and *dst* are :term:`path-like objects <path-like object>` or path names given as strings.
56: 
57:    *dst* must be the complete target file name; look at :func:`~shutil.copy`
58:    for a copy that accepts a target directory path.  If *src* and *dst*
59:    specify the same file, :exc:`SameFileError` is raised.
60: 
61:    The destination location must be writable; otherwise, an :exc:`OSError`
62:    exception will be raised. If *dst* already exists, it will be replaced.
63:    Special files such as character or block devices and pipes cannot be
64:    copied with this function.
65: 
66:    If *follow_symlinks* is false and *src* is a symbolic link,
67:    a new symbolic link will be created instead of copying the
68:    file *src* points to.
69: 
70:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copyfile src,dst shutil.copyfile
71: 
72:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
73:       :exc:`IOError` used to be raised instead of :exc:`OSError`.
74:       Added *follow_symlinks* argument.
75:       Now returns *dst*.
76: 
77:    .. versionchanged:: 3.4
78:       Raise :exc:`SameFileError` instead of :exc:`Error`.  Since the former is
79:       a subclass of the latter, this change is backward compatible.
80: 
81:    .. versionchanged:: 3.8
82:       Platform-specific fast-copy syscalls may be used internally in order to
83:       copy the file more efficiently. See
84:       :ref:`shutil-platform-dependent-efficient-copy-operations` section.
85: 
86: .. exception:: SpecialFileError
87: 
88:    This exception is raised when :func:`copyfile` or :func:`copytree` attempt
89:    to copy a named pipe.
90: 
91:    .. versionadded:: 2.7
92: 
93: .. exception:: SameFileError
94: 
95:    This exception is raised if source and destination in :func:`copyfile`
96:    are the same file.
97: 
98:    .. versionadded:: 3.4
99: 
100: 
101: .. function:: copymode(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True)
102: 
103:    Copy the permission bits from *src* to *dst*.  The file contents, owner, and
104:    group are unaffected.  *src* and *dst* are :term:`path-like objects <path-like object>` or path names
105:    given as strings.
106:    If *follow_symlinks* is false, and both *src* and *dst* are symbolic links,
107:    :func:`copymode` will attempt to modify the mode of *dst* itself (rather
108:    than the file it points to).  This functionality is not available on every
109:    platform; please see :func:`copystat` for more information.  If
110:    :func:`copymode` cannot modify symbolic links on the local platform, and it
111:    is asked to do so, it will do nothing and return.
112: 
113:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copymode src,dst shutil.copymode
114: 
115:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
116:       Added *follow_symlinks* argument.
117: 
118: .. function:: copystat(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True)
119: 
120:    Copy the permission bits, last access time, last modification time, and
121:    flags from *src* to *dst*.  On Linux, :func:`copystat` also copies the
122:    "extended attributes" where possible.  The file contents, owner, and
123:    group are unaffected.  *src* and *dst* are :term:`path-like objects <path-like object>` or path
124:    names given as strings.
125: 
126:    If *follow_symlinks* is false, and *src* and *dst* both
127:    refer to symbolic links, :func:`copystat` will operate on
128:    the symbolic links themselves rather than the files the
129:    symbolic links refer to—reading the information from the
130:    *src* symbolic link, and writing the information to the
131:    *dst* symbolic link.
132: 
133:    .. note::
134: 
135:       Not all platforms provide the ability to examine and
136:       modify symbolic links.  Python itself can tell you what
137:       functionality is locally available.
138: 
139:       * If ``os.chmod in os.supports_follow_symlinks`` is
140:         ``True``, :func:`copystat` can modify the permission
141:         bits of a symbolic link.
142: 
143:       * If ``os.utime in os.supports_follow_symlinks`` is
144:         ``True``, :func:`copystat` can modify the last access
145:         and modification times of a symbolic link.
146: 
147:       * If ``os.chflags in os.supports_follow_symlinks`` is
148:         ``True``, :func:`copystat` can modify the flags of
149:         a symbolic link.  (``os.chflags`` is not available on
150:         all platforms.)
151: 
152:       On platforms where some or all of this functionality
153:       is unavailable, when asked to modify a symbolic link,
154:       :func:`copystat` will copy everything it can.
155:       :func:`copystat` never returns failure.
156: 
157:       Please see :data:`os.supports_follow_symlinks`
158:       for more information.
159: 
160:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copystat src,dst shutil.copystat
161: 
162:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
163:       Added *follow_symlinks* argument and support for Linux extended attributes.
164: 
165: .. function:: copy(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True)
166: 
167:    Copies the file *src* to the file or directory *dst*.  *src* and *dst*
168:    should be :term:`path-like objects <path-like object>` or strings.  If
169:    *dst* specifies a directory, the file will be copied into *dst* using the
170:    base filename from *src*. If *dst* specifies a file that already exists,
171:    it will be replaced. Returns the path to the newly created file.
172: 
173:    If *follow_symlinks* is false, and *src* is a symbolic link,
174:    *dst* will be created as a symbolic link.  If *follow_symlinks*
175:    is true and *src* is a symbolic link, *dst* will be a copy of
176:    the file *src* refers to.
177: 
178:    :func:`~shutil.copy` copies the file data and the file's permission
179:    mode (see :func:`os.chmod`).  Other metadata, like the
180:    file's creation and modification times, is not preserved.
181:    To preserve all file metadata from the original, use
182:    :func:`~shutil.copy2` instead.
183: 
184:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copyfile src,dst shutil.copy
185: 
186:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copymode src,dst shutil.copy
187: 
188:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
189:       Added *follow_symlinks* argument.
190:       Now returns path to the newly created file.
191: 
192:    .. versionchanged:: 3.8
193:       Platform-specific fast-copy syscalls may be used internally in order to
194:       copy the file more efficiently. See
195:       :ref:`shutil-platform-dependent-efficient-copy-operations` section.
196: 
197: .. function:: copy2(src, dst, *, follow_symlinks=True)
198: 
199:    Identical to :func:`~shutil.copy` except that :func:`copy2`
200:    also attempts to preserve file metadata.
201: 
202:    When *follow_symlinks* is false, and *src* is a symbolic
203:    link, :func:`copy2` attempts to copy all metadata from the
204:    *src* symbolic link to the newly created *dst* symbolic link.
205:    However, this functionality is not available on all platforms.
206:    On platforms where some or all of this functionality is
207:    unavailable, :func:`copy2` will preserve all the metadata
208:    it can; :func:`copy2` never raises an exception because it
209:    cannot preserve file metadata.
210: 
211:    :func:`copy2` uses :func:`copystat` to copy the file metadata.
212:    Please see :func:`copystat` for more information
213:    about platform support for modifying symbolic link metadata.
214: 
215:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copyfile src,dst shutil.copy2
216: 
217:    .. audit-event:: shutil.copystat src,dst shutil.copy2
218: 
219:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
220:       Added *follow_symlinks* argument, try to copy extended
221:       file system attributes too (currently Linux only).
222:       Now returns path to the newly created file.
223: 
224:    .. versionchanged:: 3.8
225:       Platform-specific fast-copy syscalls may be used internally in order to
226:       copy the file more efficiently. See
227:       :ref:`shutil-platform-dependent-efficient-copy-operations` section.
228:

372: .. function:: move(src, dst, copy_function=copy2)
373: 
374:    Recursively move a file or directory (*src*) to another location and return
375:    the destination.
376: 
377:    If *dst* is an existing directory or a symlink to a directory, then *src*
378:    is moved inside that directory. The destination path in that directory must
379:    not already exist.
380: 
381:    If *dst* already exists but is not a directory, it may be overwritten
382:    depending on :func:`os.rename` semantics.
383: 
384:    If the destination is on the current filesystem, then :func:`os.rename` is
385:    used. Otherwise, *src* is copied to the destination using *copy_function*
386:    and then removed.  In case of symlinks, a new symlink pointing to the target
387:    of *src* will be created as the destination and *src* will be removed.
388: 
389:    If *copy_function* is given, it must be a callable that takes two arguments,
390:    *src* and the destination, and will be used to copy *src* to the destination
391:    if :func:`os.rename` cannot be used.  If the source is a directory,
392:    :func:`copytree` is called, passing it the *copy_function*. The
393:    default *copy_function* is :func:`copy2`.  Using :func:`~shutil.copy` as the
394:    *copy_function* allows the move to succeed when it is not possible to also
395:    copy the metadata, at the expense of not copying any of the metadata.
396: 
397:    .. audit-event:: shutil.move src,dst shutil.move
398: 
399:    .. versionchanged:: 3.3
400:       Added explicit symlink handling for foreign filesystems, thus adapting
401:       it to the behavior of GNU's :program:`mv`.
402:       Now returns *dst*.
403: 
404:    .. versionchanged:: 3.5
405:       Added the *copy_function* keyword argument.

515: .. _shutil-platform-dependent-efficient-copy-operations:
516: 
517: Platform-dependent efficient copy operations
518: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
519: 
520: Starting from Python 3.8, all functions involving a file copy
521: (:func:`copyfile`, :func:`~shutil.copy`, :func:`copy2`,
522: :func:`copytree`, and :func:`move`) may use
523: platform-specific "fast-copy" syscalls in order to copy the file more
524: efficiently (see :issue:`33671`).
525: "fast-copy" means that the copying operation occurs within the kernel, avoiding
526: the use of userspace buffers in Python as in "``outfd.write(infd.read())``".
527: 
528: On macOS `fcopyfile`_ is used to copy the file content (not metadata).
529: 
530: On Linux :func:`os.sendfile` is used.
531: 
532: On Windows :func:`shutil.copyfile` uses a bigger default buffer size (1 MiB
533: instead of 64 KiB) and a :func:`memoryview`-based variant of
534: :func:`shutil.copyfileobj` is used.
535: 
536: If the fast-copy operation fails and no data was written in the destination
537: file then shutil will silently fallback on using less efficient
538: :func:`copyfileobj` function internally.
539: 
540: .. versionchanged:: 3.8
